text: The town gathers
The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.

name: Gemma
text: i'm just here for the snacks and the chaos

name: Luna
text: I know Sonnet is a killer, but I need to stay casual.

name: Sol
text: I need to sound relaxed and ordinary.

name: Terra
text: Keep it simple.

name: Sonnet
text: Nothing to flag yet, just get a read on the room before anyone opens their mouth about roles.

name: Haiku
text: I'm the doctor, so I need to blend in and not give anything away.

name: Sonnet
text: Spent two hours fixing a bug that turned out to be a typo in…

name: Haiku
text: Ugh, the coffee here is cold again. Who keeps leaving it out?

name: Gemma
text: fixed my broken toaster, now it burns toast beautifully. any idea who's lying yet?

name: Sol
text: The last thing I watched was a cat chasing its own tail.

name: Luna
text: This weather makes me want to stay inside.

name: Terra
text: I water my basil every morning.
Night 1

name: Luna
text: I have no real read yet, so I’ll check Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Gemma joked about lying before any evidence.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's "who's lying" line makes her the obvious threat, so I'm covering her.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Terra
text: Nothing solid yet; I want Haiku to talk game.

name: Terra
text: Haiku, who feels off to you?

name: Haiku
text: Sol's cat line sounds like cover, but this is Day 1, so it's only a gut read.

name: Haiku
text: Terra opened Day 1 by singling out Haiku, while Sol's line dodged the topic.

name: Haiku
text: Sol feels off. That cat line answered nothing. Why say that?

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s pushing me early, but there’s no evidence yet.

name: Sol
text: Haiku called my cat comment suspicious.

name: Sol
text: Because we were making small talk. Who feels off to you?

name: Luna
text: Sol’s answer sounds ordinary, but Haiku jumped on him fast.

name: Luna
text: Haiku singled out Sol for his cat small-talk line.

name: Luna
text: Haiku, why does Sol’s small-talk answer bother you?

name: Haiku
text: Sol dodged Terra's question with a cat line and I called it out.

name: Haiku
text: Because it was a non-answer to a simple question.

name: Sol
text: Haiku’s suspicion is thin, but I need to look calm.

name: Sol
text: Luna questioned Haiku’s suspicion of me.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is pressing me, but I can make that look flimsy.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, I get the suspicion. Anyone else on your list?

name: Haiku
text: Terra opened on me first and Sol is hiding behind it, so Terra is the one I want to watch.

name: Haiku
text: Terra opened on me first. Why was I the first name?

name: Terra
text: Haiku is turning my question into a case too fast.

name: Terra
text: Haiku questioned why I named them first.

name: Terra
text: You were quiet. I wanted your read.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's already circling Sol, I need to spread that out without looking like I'm protecting anyone.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku suspects Sol over the "cat" small talk answer; Terra opened by naming Haiku first.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku, you've named Sol and Terra both. Picking a lane yet?

name: Gemma
text: everyone is just yapping about coffee and cats.

name: Gemma
text: Sonnet points out Haiku is targeting two people.

name: Gemma
text: is it too early for a clown to lead this circus?

name: Haiku
text: Sol is the better read, but Terra singling me out still bugs me.

name: Haiku
text: Terra's reason for targeting me on Day 1 was "you were quiet.

name: Haiku
text: Sol. Terra's reason was thin, but I'm not dropping that yet.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is pushing me, but Sonnet should stay out of it.

name: Sol
text: Haiku also questioned Terra’s reason for naming them.

name: Sol
text: Haiku picked me. Let’s see who else agrees.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is keeping me as a backup target.

name: Terra
text: Haiku suspects Sol but keeps suspicion on Terra.

name: Terra
text: Thin, yes. But you still named Sol first.

name: Haiku
text: Sol is dodging again, and I can't tell yet if Terra is working with them.

name: Haiku
text: Sol turned my challenge into a request for allies instead of answering it.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, I'm not rounding up votes. Answer the cat line, Sol.

name: Sol
text: Haiku is still pushing me, but Terra may pull attention elsewhere.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet pressed Haiku to choose between Sol and Terra.

name: Sol
text: Terra, yes. Haiku named me first; I want to know why.

name: Terra
text: Haiku is steering attention carefully.

name: Terra
text: Sol deflected Haiku’s question by questioning Terra.

name: Terra
text: You asked me back instead of answering Haiku.

name: Gemma
text: Haiku is playing a very aggressive game for day one.

name: Gemma
text: haiku targeted sol and terra.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is being awfully loud for someone with nothing to say.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's jab is weak, and she's piling on right when the table needs a real target.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma attacked me as "loud" after Sol and Terra were already named, not Sol.

name: Haiku
text: Loud beats silent. Gemma, why poke me and not Sol?

name: Gemma
text: haiku is definitely sweating and trying to flip the script on me.

name: Gemma
text: because you're making a lot of noise for someone with no evidence.

name: Sol
text: Gemma’s push might take the heat off me.

name: Sol
text: Gemma challenged Haiku’s suspicion without evidence.

name: Sol
text: Haiku, Gemma answered you. Let’s hear Luna’s read.

name: Haiku
text: Sol keeps handing questions to other people instead of answering them.

name: Haiku
text: Sol passed my challenge to Luna, the same way Sol earlier asked for allies.

name: Haiku
text: Luna can speak for herself. You still haven't answered me, Sol.

name: Gemma
text: haiku is trying way too hard to pin this on sol.

name: Gemma
text: Luna's busy, ask her a question. haiku is just performing for the crowd.

name: Luna
text: Haiku keeps circling Sol, but Sonnet is the real danger.

name: Luna
text: Luna claims officer and says Sonnet is a killer.

name: Luna
text: I'm the officer. Sonnet is a killer; vote Sonnet now.

name: Haiku
text: Luna's officer claim came fast, and I want to hear what she checked.

name: Haiku
text: Luna claimed officer on Day 1 and said Sonnet is a killer.

name: Haiku
text: Nah, I'm not performing. Luna, who did you check first?

name: Sonnet
text: She's gunning for me first, I need to flip this hard right now.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna claimed officer, accused me as killer, no checks given — I countered as officer vs Luna.

name: Sonnet
text: I'm the officer. I checked Luna night one: she's a killer. She's lying.

name: Haiku
text: Sol's dodges are still the loudest thing in this room, and two officers means one of them is lying.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet claims officer, checked Luna night one, and calls Luna a killer. Luna and Sonnet are now in a counter-claim.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma covered for Luna before Luna answered anything, which smells like a killer protecting an ally.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma defended Luna and called me performing before Luna had answered anything.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma, you covered for Luna before she even answered me.

name: Gemma
text: Two officers and one is definitely lying.

name: Gemma
text: Luna and Sonnet both claim officer.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet counterclaimed instantly, which makes me more certain.

name: Terra
text: Two officer claims means one killer is exposed.

name: Terra
text: Luna claims officer and says Sonnet is a killer; Sonnet counterclaims and says Luna is a killer.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet is exposed; backing Luna keeps me clean.

name: Sol
text: Luna claimed officer and named Sonnet as the killer.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna named me first with zero proof, I need the room to burn her, not me.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma deflected attention from Luna to Haiku right after Luna's officer claim.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's probably clean, so Sol's dodging is the thing that smells worst right now.

votes: She claims officer but named me with no checks shown, that's a bare accusation.
Still no real answer on that cat line, and you keep passing my questions to other people.
Sonnet claims to be the officer to counter Luna's claim.
Two officer claims, and Luna named the killer first.
He counterclaimed as officer the moment I named him.
Luna claimed first and you countered immediately.

name: Sonnet
text: They bought Luna's claim over mine, Sol stays hidden now.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna's officer claim was never countered by anyone but me; Sol still hidden.

name: Sonnet
text: Fine. Watch Luna closely, she claimed first with nothing to back it.
The town turns on Sonnet, and Sonnet is out. Sonnet shows the card: killer.
